common rust.description: Common rust of corn appears as small, round to elongate reddish-brown pustules on both leaf surfaces. These pustules often appear in bands on the leaves.
treatment: Apply fungicides such as mancozeb or azoxystrobin when rust first appears, especially on susceptible hybrids.
Spray systemic fungicides (e.g., tebuconazole, propiconazole) if the infection is severe and conditions favor its spread.
prevention: Plant corn hybrids that are resistant or tolerant to common rust.
Rotate crops to reduce the amount of fungal inoculum in the soil.
Ensure proper plant spacing to improve air circulation within the crop canopy.
fertilizer_recommendation: Apply 120–150 kg Nitrogen, 60–75 kg Phosphorus (P2O5), and 40–60 kg Potassium (K2O) per hectare.
Split the nitrogen application into 2–3 doses (at planting, knee-high, and tasseling) to provide consistent nutrition without making the plant overly succulent.
soil_recommendation: Best grown in well-drained loamy soils.
Avoid waterlogging, which can weaken the plant and make it more susceptible to disease.

cercospora leaf spot gray.description: Gray leaf spot is characterized by small, rectangular or long, narrow lesions on the leaves that are gray-tan in color. These lesions often appear in humid conditions.
treatment: Apply fungicides containing strobilurins (e.g., azoxystrobin) or triazoles (e.g., propiconazole) when lesions first appear on the lower leaves.
Follow a regular spray schedule if conditions remain favorable for the disease.
prevention: Practice crop rotation with non-host crops (e.g., soybeans, wheat).
Plow under infected corn residue after harvest to reduce the fungal inoculum for the next season.
fertilizer_recommendation: Apply 120–150 kg Nitrogen, 60–75 kg Phosphorus (P2O5), and 40–60 kg Potassium (K2O) per hectare.
Proper fertilization strengthens the plant's natural defense mechanisms.
soil_recommendation: Thrives in well-drained, fertile loamy soils.
Maintain a soil pH between 5.8 and 7.0.

healthy.description: A healthy corn plant has strong, vibrant green leaves and stalks, is free from any visible lesions, spots, or signs of pests, and shows robust growth.
treatment: Maintain a consistent irrigation and fertilization schedule.
Regularly scout the field to detect any disease or pest issues early.
prevention: Plant corn hybrids with high disease resistance ratings.
Implement good field sanitation and crop rotation practices.
fertilizer_recommendation: Apply 120–150 kg Nitrogen, 60–75 kg Phosphorus (P2O5), and 40–60 kg Potassium (K2O) per hectare.
Split nitrogen application to match the corn's growth stages.
soil_recommendation: Grows best in well-drained, fertile loamy soils.

northern leaf blight.description: Northern leaf blight causes long, cigar-shaped, gray-green or tan lesions on the leaves, starting on the lower leaves and moving up the plant.
treatment: Apply fungicides such as mancozeb, propiconazole, or azoxystrobin when symptoms first appear.
Fungicide application is most critical to protect the ear leaf and leaves above it during the reproductive stages.
prevention: Plant corn hybrids with a high resistance rating to northern leaf blight.
Use tillage to bury corn residue from previous seasons, as the fungus overwinters in the residue.
fertilizer_recommendation: Apply 120–150 kg Nitrogen, 60–75 kg Phosphorus (P2O5), and 40–60 kg Potassium (K2O) per hectare.
Adequate fertilization, especially potassium, can help the plant better tolerate the disease.
soil_recommendation: Avoid fields with a history of the disease if possible.
